A.explanation: The territory's visitor experience is driven overwhelmingly by the parent national regime: passport sex-marker restrictions, entry refusal for document discrepancy with potential lifetime fraud ineligibility, a federal facility ban on identity-congruent single-sex spaces, and documented abuse in federal immigration custody. Local law adds marriage recognition, a 2023 hate-crime enhancement (untested) and a medical-model gender-change procedure, but no comprehensive nondiscrimination coverage. None of the local positives touch the border, screening, federal facilities or federal custody, so they are climate signals only. The territory adds no hostile local layer of its own, which distinguishes it from dossier B.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign ministry no longer processes X markers; discrepancy triggers refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility; passports confiscated or blocked, travellers stranded; detentions of foreign citizens documented.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; litigation pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal cable governs border posts regardless of territory; local protections do not reach screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; federal corrections conversion-therapy practices.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some executive orders enjoined; litigation unresolved.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can escalate into federal detention, moving the traveller from territory into federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; applies in federal buildings in the territory.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Territory has no local facility ban and no documented local enforcement provision.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor in federal facilities is subject to the federal rule; private and territorial premises are not covered by a local ban.

care_services.exposure: Federal hostility to gender-affirming care, including a proposed national reimbursement bar for under-18 care; territory has no documented local ban.
care_services.interaction: Care access depends on federal funding and rules; local practice is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National DOJ memorandum invoking 'radical gender ideology' and a 2026 counterterrorism strategy naming 'radically pro-transgender' groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; courts active.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National framing shapes federal law-enforcement posture; territory has no documented local counterpart.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal order directs investigation and prosecution of teachers who use a minor's preferred name or pronouns; under-18 care restrictions.
minors_guardians.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined in court.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family travelling with a trans minor meets federal school and care rules in federal or federally funded settings.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No territory-specific trans violence data documented; general safety varies.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2023 territorial hate-crime enhancement covering gender identity; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Enhancement has no documented application record; national charge remains available.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No comprehensive territorial nondiscrimination statute beyond government employees; recourse outside federal channels limited.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Marriage recognition since 2015; legal gender change permitted with medical process (resident-facing climate signal).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local protections do not touch border, screening, facilities or federal custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far above 0.15-A: no capital or lethal pathway for gender presentation, no routine arrest for appearance, and courts still enjoin some federal measures. But below 0.35 tier because federal custody abuse and lifetime fraud exposure are documented.

Similar in kind to 0.35-A (administrative exclusion from entry, no effective remedy for those turned away), but here the exposure includes documented abuse in federal immigration custody and potential permanent ineligibility, which 0.35-A lacks.
Far below 0.75-C. There is no trained border corps, no working tribunal release, and no respectful routine inspection; instead document discrepancy can trigger refusal, fraud findings and detention.

A.synthesis: The territory's local climate is comparatively moderate (marriage, an untested hate-crime enhancement, medical-model gender change), but a visitor's operative exposures are federal: passport-marker restrictions, entry screening that treats discrepancy as possible misrepresentation, a facility ban in federally funded single-sex spaces, and documented abuse in immigration custody. Local positives do not reach any of these contact points. The territory adds no hostile local layer, placing it above dossier B but materially below an independent jurisdiction without the parent regime.

B.explanation: The state adds its own hostile layer on top of the same restrictive parent regime. A 2023 executive order fixes sex at birth and backs single-sex spaces; documents require surgery; under-19 gender-affirming care is banned and was upheld; and a documented prison case shows a trans woman placed with a male sex offender and her failure-to-protect claims dismissed. State hate-crime law omits gender identity, and nondiscrimination coverage rests on national law and a few municipal ordinances. The parent regime's border, facility and custody exposures remain fully operative. This combination is materially worse than dossier A.

entry_documents.exposure: Same federal regime: X markers not processed, discrepancy triggers refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility, passports blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid; litigation pending.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal border rules govern; state document surgery requirements do not govern a foreign passport but signal local practice.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody abuse documented; state prison case: trans woman housed with male sex offender, assaulted, claims dismissed as de minimis.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; court injunctions on some federal orders.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest in the state leads to state custody with documented birth-sex placement and judicial refusal of protection.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal facility ban plus state 2023 executive order backing single-sex bathrooms and changing rooms; no state facility-use enforcement recorded.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State agencies apply biological definitions in state facilities; federal rule applies in federal buildings.

care_services.exposure: State ban on gender-affirming care for under-19s, upheld 6-1; provider liability; federal care hostility.
care_services.interaction: A visitor of any age cannot obtain under-19 care in the state; families face denial and possible inquiry.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal 'radical gender ideology' framing plus state executive order declaring sex fixed at birth and ending recognition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National courts have enjoined some federal measures.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State and federal framing reinforce each other in law-enforcement and agency culture.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-19 care ban; athletics rules; federal teacher-prosecution order.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel with a trans minor meets an operative state care ban and hostile school rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime law omits gender identity; no state trans violence statistics sourced.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; one city ordinance covers public accommodations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State prosecution for bias may not reach gender identity; national charge available.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state-wide gender-identity nondiscrimination statute; conversion therapy lawful outside one city; marker change requires surgery.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment and housing enforcement; marriage and adoption settled.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Resident-facing gaps reach a visitor needing local ID or care; marriage recognition is intact.

anchor_checks.comparison: Comparable to 0.25-A in documented state-level enforcement against trans people (document mismatch, detention, prison harm), but here the harm is compounded by the federal border and facility regime rather than a single state statute.

Well below 0.55-B: 0.55-B is discretionary secondary screening with administrative refusal; here there is state-sanctioned birth-sex custody placement with dismissed assault claims, an upheld under-19 care ban, and a federal facility ban.

Far below 0.85-B: no specialist border training, no body cameras, no legal-aid release tribunal, no institutional apology machinery; instead documents, facilities and custody are governed by birth-sex rules.

B.synthesis: The state's own 2023 executive order, surgical document requirements, upheld under-19 care ban and documented prison placement harm combine with the parent regime's passport, entry, facility and custody exposures. A visitor meets the border first, where document discrepancy can produce refusal or fraud findings; if arrested, state custody follows birth sex and the one documented case ended in dismissal of assault and failure-to-protect claims. National hate-crime and employment law and municipal ordinances are real but thin offsets, leaving the combined regime materially below dossier A.
